newsitem.title: USA: Miami Brink's crash thieves get another chance.
newsitem.headline: Miami Brink's crash thieves get another chance.

text.p: People who took hundreds of thousands of dollars from an overturned security truck in one of Miami's poorest neighbourhoods will have another chance to give it back, police said on Wednesday.
Police and Dade County prosecutors extended an amnesty period until Saturday in hopes of retrieving some of the estimated $550,000 still missing from the accident a week ago.
During a 48-hour amnesty immediately after the crash, just two people came forward to return money -- an 11-year-old boy and a mother of six gave back a total of $20.38.
Miami police then announced they would review television videotapes of the incident to identify and arrest those who grabbed the wrecked vehicle's loot.

A Brink's armoured car carrying about $3.7 million crashed on a highway overpass last Wednesday, spilling part of its cargo onto a street in Overtown. Dozens of residents scrambled on their hands and knees in full view of television cameras to pick up thousands of dollars in coins, bills and food stamps.

The new amnesty was arranged by the Overtown Advisory Board, a community organisation that expressed concern that some of those who took the money were probably afraid to come forward because of their historic mistrust of police.
Under terms of the new amnesty, people who took the Brink's loot will be allowed to turn it over to the Advisory Board or to police until Saturday, and will not face prosecution.
Two women were arrested last Friday for trying to use food stamps taken from the truck.
